new_statements.translation: Duungoma is a tonal language, but I did not try to transcribe the tones, so tonal differences do not figure in this analysis. It is possible that, if the melodic contour of each word were written down, some of the lengthened vowels would turn out to be sequences of two short vowels with distinct tones.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only reachable first-hand prosodic remark: Duungooma is tonal; the survey author did not analyse tone and says nothing at all about stress or accent. No placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.domain_note: Survey wordlists (304 items) from Kaï, Siéou, Bananso, Zantiguila (Mali) and Samogohiri/Samogogouan (Burkina); not a phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: Hochstetler's survey treats Mali Duun (duun1242, dux: Kaï/Siéou/Bananso/Zantiguila) and Burkina Dzùùngoo (dzuu1241, dnn: Samogohiri/Samogogouan) as one 'duungoma'; his tonal remark covers both. Solomiac 2007/2014 describes only Dzùùngoo of Samogohiri (dzuu1241), a sister variety not mutually intelligible with Mali Duun per Vydrin 2017, so it cannot stand in for duun1242. DNAFLA 1981 describes the Siéou(kourani) parler and Eenkhoorn 2005 the Kaï area — both within duun1242.

tone_statements.citation: Eenkhoorn-Pilon, Jacqueline, Ibrahima Sogodogo & Djakalia Sogodogo. 2011. Lisons le duungooma: pour ceux qui savent déjà lire et écrire en français (guide d'orthographe). 2ème édition expérimentale, août 2011; orthographe préliminaire révisée (2010). Sikasso: Société Internationale de Linguistique (SIL Mali). 27 pp. [first-edition date not stated in the document; fr.wikipedia gives 2001]
tone_statements.quote: En cttmfnnl`, comme dans beaucoup d’autres langues africaines, des mots de sens très différents peuvent s’écrire avec les mêmes lettres. Pourtant ils ne se confondent pas. La raison est qu’ils se distinguent par la hauteur musicale sur laquelle on les prononce. On note cette mélodie en utilisant l'accent aigu [´] pour le ton haut, et grave [`] pour le ton bas. Si rien n’est noté, le ton est moyen. [...] Les mots en deux syllabes peuvent même avoir quatre mélodies différentes ! bas-bas / moyen-moyen² / haut-haut / bas-moyen/haut [...] ² Au niveau sous jacent, il s’agit d’une suite bas-haut (BH), qui se réalise comme ton moyen.
tone_statements.translation: In Duungooma, as in many other African languages, words of very different meaning can be written with the same letters. Yet they are not confused. The reason is that they are distinguished by the musical pitch on which they are pronounced. This melody is noted with the acute accent for high tone and the grave for low tone. If nothing is marked, the tone is mid. [...] Two-syllable words can even have four different melodies! low-low / mid-mid² / high-high / low-mid/high [...] ² At the underlying level this is a low-high (LH) sequence, which is realised as mid tone.
